page: Amazon Web Services r7i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs. Network connectivity is supported by a 38 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

The hardware configuration delivers strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 84,975.32 and a PassMark CPU score of 87,164.85, which places it in the top tier. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 228.17 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 95.44 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance achieves 30,332.14 operations on PassMark and 98.08 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It also shows strong capabilities in cryptographic operations and image processing, though single-core stress-ng performance and PassMark memory scores remain in the average tier.

The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy tasks despite the 38 Gbps network baseline. However, the high density of DDR5 memory and dedicated Intel Xeon cores offer qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by reducing the need to scale horizontally. This instance is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks where high memory capacity and memory bandwidth are critical.
